:::::: bs-page-shell
::::: bs-reading-column
Technology Commons is an open teaching project for learning technology by designing, building, testing, explaining, and improving real work.

The idea is simple:

> **Come with a question. Leave with something you understand well enough to use, test, build, or explain.**

The site brings lessons, projects, tools, references, classroom routines, and research into one shared place for technology education.

## Why We Built This

Technology courses move constantly between thinking and doing. A student may need to understand a measurement, make a sketch, write code, diagnose a fault, choose a material, use a machine, test an idea, and explain what happened, sometimes all in the same project.

Technology Commons is designed around the kinds of questions that appear while doing that work:

::: bs-question-examples
[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *How do I turn an idea into something that actually works?*

[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *How precise does this measurement need to be, and which tool should I use?*

[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *Why did this prototype, program, circuit, or repair fail, and what should I change next?*

[\>]{.bs-code-prefix aria-hidden="true"} *How can I show the decisions, evidence, and learning behind the finished result?*

[// goal: learn by making, testing, explaining, and improving]{.bs-code-note}
:::

The aim is not to separate theory from practice. It is to build clear mental models through real work, then use evidence from that work to improve the next attempt.

::: bs-section-heading
## Technology Commons

[ROLE: CLASSROOM :: WORKSHOP :: COMMONS]{.bs-heading-meta}
:::

Technology Commons supports three secondary technology course groups: **TAS2O Exploring Technologies**, **TEJ3M / TEJ4M Computer Engineering Technology**, and **TTJ3C / TTJ4C Transportation Technology**.

Each course has its own pathway, but they share common ideas: safe work, measurement, design, technical communication, iteration, evidence, reflection, and the responsibility to leave useful knowledge behind for others.

The word **commons** is intentional. Useful knowledge should be shared, inspected, improved, and reused. Students should be able to find what they need today, while educators should be able to inspect the structure and adapt what is useful elsewhere.

## A Shared Design Process

Projects use the NICE cycle:

**Needs & Necessities -> Investigate & Inquire -> Create & Communicate -> Evaluate -> repeat**

NICE is not a one-way checklist. Evaluation can reveal a new need, a misunderstood constraint, a better question, or a better design. The cycle begins again with better information.

## Port Credit roots

Technology Commons is built for teaching at Port Credit Secondary School, and its visual identity deliberately connects to the school without trying to replace the school's own identity.

Port Credit's secondary-school history reaches back to **1919**, when a continuation school opened in the community. The PCSS Alumni Association preserves school history, yearbooks, memorabilia, and stories while supporting scholarships and selected school projects.

The **Regional SciTech Program launched in September 2005**. Alumni material describes it as an integrated science and technology program intended for both inquiry-oriented academic learners and hands-on learners interested in college, apprenticeships, skilled trades, and industry.

These ideas fit the Commons well: practical work, technical knowledge, curiosity, community, and leaving useful knowledge behind.

- [PCSS Alumni Association](https://www.pcssalumni.com/)
- [PCSS Alumni - School Programs and SciTech history](https://www.pcssalumni.com/school-programs/)
- [PCSS Alumni - Yearbook archive information](https://www.pcssalumni.com/yearbooks-on-cd/)
- [1960 yearbook history of Port Credit High School](https://www.pcssalumni.com/PDF/YB-1960.pdf)

## Brand system

The Technology Commons brand is meant to feel **sleek, structured, technical, calm, and distinctly Port Credit**. The visual language draws from the school and SciTech marks, the lighthouse, Lake Ontario, the harbour, the Credit River, shoreline materials, and the school's blue-and-gold identity. Deep neutrals keep the system restrained. Wellness greens add balance and calm. Purple supports reflection and creativity, while red is reserved for genuinely important emphasis.

The goal is not to reproduce every historical PCSS colour exactly. The Commons uses a coherent working palette that feels related to Port Credit while remaining flexible enough for websites, slides, diagrams, classroom tools, and technical material.

This is the working official palette for Technology Commons. It is **not** a claim that every colour below is an official Port Credit Secondary School colour.

These are the foundation colours for text, backgrounds, dividers, diagrams, and interface surfaces. The names reference the local waterfront rather than a separate visual theme.

### Source colours from supplied PCSS marks

The supplied files do not all use exactly the same blue and yellow. That is useful historical context, but the logos themselves should not be recoloured just to force them into the Commons palette.

| Source mark | Blue | Yellow / gold |
|---|---|---|
| Warriors roundel | `#1D2347` | `#FCD937` |
| Newer SciTech roundel | `#19226D` | `#FFCF01` |
| Older Regional SciTech mark | `#464780` | `#F0DB7C` |

### Recommended combinations

| Mode | Use |
|---|---|
| **Commons core** | Lighthouse Black + Sail White + Port Credit Navy + Technical Blue |
| **Wellness** | Lighthouse Black + Sail White + Credit River Moss + Sea Glass |
| **Port Credit spirit** | Port Credit Navy + PCSS Yellow + Sail White |
| **SciTech** | SciTech Navy + Technical Blue + SciTech Gold |
| **Harbour** | Harbour Charcoal + Lake Mist + Harbour Blue + Copper |
| **Reflection / creativity** | Lighthouse Black + Sail White + Iris Purple |
| **Urgent / important** | Lighthouse Black + Sail White + Beacon Red, used sparingly |

A page or slide should normally use one mode, not the full palette at once.

### Logo use

Keep the supplied proportions and colours. Do not stretch, skew, add effects, or casually recolour school marks. When possible, use transparent source files rather than extracting logos from screenshots.

Technology Commons can sit beside these marks, but it should not imply that every Commons page or resource is an official publication of Port Credit Secondary School or the Peel District School Board.

## Built to Be Useful

Technology Commons should be useful first. A student should be able to open the site during class, find the right course or tool, and continue working without needing to understand how the site itself is organized.
